xBRIEFInfo.description: Project definition -- current Deft Directive identity, policy, scope registry, and authored architecture metadata.

narratives.Overview: Deft Directive is a self-dogfooded framework for AI-assisted software work. It combines agent-consumed guidance, deterministic Taskfile automation, vBRIEF lifecycle metadata, a TypeScript engine, OVPR npm packages (Go installer deleted), local triage/cache workflows, content packs, and release/PR gates. The current source tree is Taskfile-first: `task --list` is the primary command contract, delegating to the TypeScript engine in `packages/`. The legacy Python runtime and the `run`/`run.py`/`run.bat` launchers were fully removed at v0.63.0 -- deft is now TypeScript-native end to end. Project identity and architectural intent live in `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`; rendered markdown files such as `SPECIFICATION.md`, `PRD.md`, and `ROADMAP.md` are generated views. The early Deft intent remains active: turn loose agent prompting into a repeatable practice with modular guidance, lazy loading, specification before implementation, observable tests/gates, and a feedback loop for lessons learned.
narratives.Architecture: The implemented architecture has ten cooperating areas. (1) Framework content: `AGENTS.md`, `main.md`, standards, skills, strategies, templates, docs, conventions, and domain guidance consumed by agents. (2) Task runner: `Taskfile.yml` and `tasks/*.yml` expose the deterministic command surface for checks, rendering, lifecycle, triage, scope, cache, release, PR, swarm, policy, packs, and codebase commands. (3) TypeScript engine: `packages/` plus root package metadata and TS configs implement the deterministic gates, CLI shims, command routing, validators, renderers, lifecycle movement, issue/cache/triage automation, doctor/session gates, and codebase extraction -- the primary tooling runtime. The #1530 Python-to-TypeScript migration completed at v0.63.0: the Python runtime, `scripts/*.py`, and the `run`/`run.py`/`run.bat` launchers were removed and the Python-oracle parity harnesses retired. (4) Node workspace and build: `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `tsconfig*.json`, and the `vitest` config define the workspace, build, and test-runner surface for the engine. (5) Install/upgrade (OVPR / AC10.10): global `@deftai/directive` + project `@deftai/directive-runtime` via `directive install` / `upgrade` / `install --repair` / `uninstall` / `doctor`. The Go installer (`cmd/deft-install/`) is **deleted** — do not teach it as current. (6) vBRIEF metadata: `xbrief/` stores project identity, specification source, schemas, lifecycle scope files, policy, and `plan.architecture.codeStructure`. (7) Triage/cache/scope automation: `.deft-cache/`, `xbrief/.eval/`, `task triage:*`, `task cache:*`, and `task scope:*` turn GitHub/backlog state into auditable scope vBRIEFs. (8) Release/PR/swarm automation: `task release:*`, `task pr:*`, `task swarm:*`, and associated skills encode pre-PR, review, merge, and release workflows. (9) Codebase architecture metadata: `codeStructure` is the authored source of truth; `task codebase:validate-structure`, `codebase:extract-default`, `codebase:provider-map`, `codebase:map`, `verify:codebase-map-fresh`, and `codebase:projection-registry` implement the current contract and MAP projection layer. (10) Tests and gates: colocated `packages/**/*.test.ts` suites plus shared fixtures and snapshots under `tests/`, `.githooks/`, `.github/workflows/`, and `task check` provide regression, content, branch, encoding, vBRIEF, capacity, session, and forward-coverage enforcement.
narratives.ProblemStatement: The framework has outgrown its early self-specification. The old project narratives described a four-component, Phase 1-3 system centered on Markdown content, the `run` CLI, the Go installer, and tests. That no longer matches the implemented command surface or operational model. Current contributors need docs that reflect Taskfile-first automation, `.deft/core` installation, vBRIEF lifecycle state, triage/cache/scope workflows, content packs, release/PR automation, and codebase-structure projection contracts without flattening the original method-oriented intent behind Deft.
narratives.Goals:
1. Keep vBRIEF sources authoritative and generated markdown clearly derivative.
2. Present `task` (delegating to the TypeScript engine in `packages/`) as the primary deterministic command surface.
3. Document the actual implemented modules: framework content, Taskfile tasks, the TypeScript engine, OVPR install packages (Go installer deleted), vBRIEF metadata, triage/cache/scope, release/PR/swarm automation, content packs, codebase contracts, and tests.
4. Preserve the early Deft mental model: modular guidance, lazy loading, TDD/SDD, small reversible scopes, and self-improving standards.
5. Use diagrams where process flow matters, especially session rituals, implementation gates, lifecycle movement, source/projection boundaries, and triage/cache flow.
6. Keep the codebase MAP distinction accurate: `.planning/codebase/MAP.md` is generated and freshness-checked, while `plan.architecture.codeStructure` remains canonical.
7. Remove or label stale Phase 1-3 and v0.5-era narratives so agents do not treat historical text as current authority.
narratives.UserStories:
**US-1** -- As a contributor, I want the project definition and architecture docs to describe the actual implemented system so I can orient quickly without reverse-engineering Taskfiles and scripts.

**US-2** -- As an agent, I want source-of-truth and generated-view boundaries to be explicit so I update vBRIEF sources instead of editing rendered markdown by hand.

**US-3** -- As a maintainer, I want docs to name current gates and command namespaces so PRs run the same checks that CI and branch policy expect.

**US-4** -- As a framework user, I want install and upgrade docs to point at `.deft/core` and the canonical installer/doctor handoff instead of legacy clone assumptions.

**US-5** -- As a MAP reader, I want codebase-structure docs to explain which facts are canonical, which are provider/default-derived, and how freshness is checked.

**US-6** -- As a reader learning Deft, I want diagrams and concept sections that explain the process flow and original intent behind the framework, not just an inventory of implemented files.
narratives.NonFunctionalRequirements:
- **NFR-1**: `task check` remains the authoritative pre-commit quality gate for the directive repository.
- **NFR-2**: xBRIEF files must validate as schema version `0.8` (legacy 0.6 remains read-accepted); v0.5 references are historical only.
- **NFR-3**: Markdown render outputs (`SPECIFICATION.md`, `PRD.md`, `ROADMAP.md`) must keep generated banners and source-of-truth pointers.
- **NFR-4**: `codeStructure` must contain authored intent only, not derived facts such as imports, symbols, file counts, or dependency graphs.
- **NFR-5**: Installer docs must preserve the current `.deft/core` vendored-layout contract and legacy-layout back-compat distinction.
narratives.SuccessMetrics:
- Project-definition and specification narratives describe the current architecture rather than the early Phase 1-3 shape.
- `SPECIFICATION.md` is regenerated from `xbrief/specification.xbrief.json` and opens with current system context.
- Architecture, concepts, files, commands, README, and codebase docs agree on Taskfile-first operation and vBRIEF source-of-truth boundaries.
- Architecture/concepts/commands docs include current Mermaid diagrams for rituals, gates, lifecycle, projections, and triage/cache flow.
- Stale planning docs cannot be mistaken for current architecture guidance.
- Validation commands for vBRIEF and codeStructure pass after the documentation refresh.
narratives.OpenQuestions:
1. **Generated source headers** -- the MAP generator, freshness gate, and PR6 consumer guidance are complete. Generated source headers remain a split optional projection follow-up; local indexes and materialized views are tracked separately by #1618.
2. **Runtime decoupling** -- the legacy `run` CLI and the Python runtime were removed at v0.63.0; the TypeScript engine in `packages/` is the sole runtime, invoked through the Taskfile command graph. The long-term split between framework guidance, package-manager command routing, and the Taskfile runtime is still evolving through scoped work.
3. **Content-pack UX** -- `packs:*` tasks exist, but the public documentation should continue to expand as the pack format becomes a primary user-facing surface.
narratives.ProjectConfig:
# Deft Directive Project Guidelines

Legend (from RFC2119): !=MUST, ~=SHOULD, ≉=SHOULD NOT, ⊗=MUST NOT, ?=MAY.

Only specify items here that override or extend the framework defaults.

## Project Configuration

**Tech Stack**: Markdown guidance and vBRIEF JSON for agent-consumed state; a TypeScript/Node engine (`packages/`) for validators, renderers, and gates; OVPR npm launcher/runtime (Go installer deleted); Taskfile command graph; content packs; GitHub Actions and local hooks for gates.

**Primary command contract**: `task --list` and the root/task include graph. Key namespaces include `check`, `verify:*`, `vbrief:*`, `spec:*`, `project:*`, `scope:*`, `triage:*`, `cache:*`, `codebase:*`, `packs:*`, `pr:*`, `release:*`, `swarm:*`, `policy:*`, and `capacity:*`.

**Source of truth**: Project identity, policy, scope registry, and authored architecture metadata live in `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`. Project specification source lives in `xbrief/specification.xbrief.json`. Rendered markdown is derivative.

**Workflow**:

```bash
task --list                  # Discover supported commands
task check                   # Pre-commit quality gate
task vbrief:validate         # Validate vBRIEF structure and lifecycle consistency
task codebase:validate-structure # Validate authored codeStructure metadata
task spec:render             # Regenerate SPECIFICATION.md from vBRIEF source
```

## Standards

- ! Run `task check` before commits.
- ! Update vBRIEF sources before generated markdown views.
- ! Keep generated projection docs clearly marked; treat `.planning/codebase/MAP.md` as derivative and refresh it with `task codebase:map`.
narratives.tech stack: Agent guidance and documentation, xBRIEF 0.8 JSON metadata, a TypeScript/Node engine (`packages/`), OVPR npm packages (Go installer deleted), Taskfile automation, content packs, Git/GitHub workflows, and GitHub Actions.

modules.name: Framework Content
modules.purpose: Agent-consumed guidance in the Content Manifest content bucket under content/, plus root harness entries AGENTS.md, main.md, and SKILL.md. Root docs/, meta/, and incidents/ are repo-dev and are not this module. content/packs is owned by content-packs. content/.agents skill copies and content/secrets placeholders are out of this module.

modules.name: TypeScript Engine
modules.purpose: Node/TypeScript packages implementing the directive engine: deterministic gates, validators, renderers, lifecycle movement, triage/cache/scope automation, doctor/session gates, codebase extraction, and CLI command routing. The sole runtime after the #1530 Python-to-TypeScript migration completed at v0.63.0 (Python tooling and parity harnesses retired).

modules.name: Task Runner
modules.purpose: Taskfile entry points that expose framework commands in source and consumer installs.

modules.name: vBRIEF Metadata
modules.purpose: Structured project, scope, schema, lifecycle, and architecture metadata.

modules.name: Content Packs
modules.purpose: Versioned JSON content packs under content/packs (JSON-only; not markdown, not mixed with repo-dev docs).

modules.name: CI and Release Automation
modules.purpose: Repository automation for branch policy, hooks, GitHub Actions, PR readiness, and release publication.

modules.name: Test Suite
modules.purpose: Shared test fixtures, snapshots, golden files, and documentation; behavioral tests are colocated under `packages/` as `*.test.ts`.

pathOwnership.rationale: Canonical codeStructure intent lives only at plan.architecture.codeStructure.
The codeStructure type surface is part of the core PROJECT-DEFINITION schema.

allowedPatterns.name: Profile before projection
allowedPatterns.description: Define and validate authored codeStructure metadata before adding extractors, MAP generation, local indexes, or generated headers.

allowedPatterns.name: Explicit validator
allowedPatterns.description: Metadata validators use explicit TypeScript parsing and checks rather than adding a runtime JSON Schema dependency.

allowedPatterns.name: Taskfile command contract
allowedPatterns.description: `task --list` is the discoverable deterministic command surface; scripts implement behavior behind task targets rather than replacing the contract.

allowedPatterns.name: Source-of-truth projection boundary
allowedPatterns.description: Authored metadata lives in vBRIEF; rendered markdown, roadmap exports, and codebase maps are generated views with explicit regeneration commands.

allowedPatterns.name: OVPR exact runtime pin
allowedPatterns.description: Supported installs use the thin `@deftai/directive` launcher plus an exact `@deftai/directive-runtime` project pin; legacy `.deft/core` clone layouts are upgrade/migration inputs only.
